## Solution

We compute the asymptotic behavior of

$$I_n = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi} \frac{\cos(2nx)}{1+x^{8}}\,dx$$

as $n\to\infty$ (through integers, so that $\sin(2n\pi)=0$), via repeated integration by parts.

Let $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{1+x^{8}}$ and $\lambda=2n$. Two integrations by parts give the standard identity

$$\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f(x)\cos(\lambda x)\,dx
= \Bigl[\tfrac{f(x)\sin(\lambda x)}{\lambda}\Bigr]_{-\pi}^{\pi}
+ \Bigl[\tfrac{f'(x)\cos(\lambda x)}{\lambda^{2}}\Bigr]_{-\pi}^{\pi}
- \frac{1}{\lambda^{2}}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f''(x)\cos(\lambda x)\,dx.$$

**First boundary term.** Since $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\sin(2n\pi)=\sin(-2n\pi)=0$, so this term vanishes.

**Second boundary term.** Using $\cos(2n\pi)=\cos(-2n\pi)=1$,

$$\Bigl[\tfrac{f'(x)\cos(2nx)}{4n^{2}}\Bigr]_{-\pi}^{\pi}
= \frac{f'(\pi)-f'(-\pi)}{4n^{2}}.$$

Since $f$ is even, $f'$ is odd, hence $f'(-\pi)=-f'(\pi)$, giving

$$\frac{f'(\pi)-f'(-\pi)}{4n^{2}}=\frac{2f'(\pi)}{4n^{2}}=\frac{f'(\pi)}{2n^{2}}.$$

Now $f'(x)=-\dfrac{8x^{7}}{(1+x^{8})^{2}}$, so

$$f'(\pi)=-\frac{8\pi^{7}}{(1+\pi^{8})^{2}}.$$

**Remainder.** Let $R_n=-\dfrac{1}{4n^{2}}\displaystyle\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f''(x)\cos(2nx)\,dx$. Since $f$ is even, $f''$ is even and $f'''$ is odd. Applying the same two-step integration by parts to $\int f''\cos(2nx)\,dx$: the $[f''\sin/(2n)]$ boundary term vanishes, and

$$\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f''(x)\cos(2nx)\,dx
= \frac{f'''(\pi)-f'''(-\pi)}{4n^{2}}+O(n^{-4})
= \frac{2f'''(\pi)}{4n^{2}}+O(n^{-4})=O(n^{-2}).$$

Therefore $R_n = O(n^{-4})$.

**Assembling.**

$$I_n = \frac{f'(\pi)}{2n^{2}} + O(n^{-4})
= -\frac{8\pi^{7}}{2n^{2}(1+\pi^{8})^{2}}+O(n^{-4})
= -\frac{4\pi^{7}}{n^{2}(1+\pi^{8})^{2}}+O(n^{-4}).$$

Multiplying by $n^{3}$:

$$n^{3}I_n
= -\frac{4n\,\pi^{7}}{(1+\pi^{8})^{2}}+O(n^{-1})
\;\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\; -\infty.$$

The leading coefficient $-\dfrac{4\pi^{7}}{(1+\pi^{8})^{2}}$ is strictly negative, so $n^{3}I_n\to -\infty$.

$$\boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{3}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\frac{\cos(2nx)}{1+x^{8}}\,dx = -\infty.}$$
